processing: A flat-shaped green tea from young buds, fixed by heat and pressed flat and straight during drying, as with other flat bud greens.
harvest_season: Spring, as with other bud-picked Jiangsu greens; the earliest buds are usually the most prized.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight, even buds in a vivid green with visible down.
appearance_wet: Plump, tender, bright green buds that stand upright in the glass before sinking.
taste_profile: A young, tender aroma and a fresh, mellow, fairly rich taste.

brewing.notes: Use a tall glass to watch the buds stand and sink. These are usual settings for a flat bud green; hotter water brings out grassiness.

vintage_note: Sold as the current spring harvest, like other Jiangsu famous greens, and best within a year of picking. The earliest buds usually cost the most, and it should not be kept for ageing.
description:
Jinshan Cuiya is a modern green tea from Zhenjiang on the Yangtze, named after the city's famous Jinshan temple hill. It is a bud tea with a flat, straight shape that recalls Long Jing at a glance.

The buds are flat, even and vivid green with visible down. Brew them in a glass and they stand upright before sinking, which local writers like to compare to the Jinshan pagoda reflected in the river.

The taste is fresh, mellow and fairly rich, with a young, tender aroma. Water around 80 °C keeps it sweet; boiling water will make a flat bud tea turn grassy quickly.

It is mainly a regional tea and turns up less often outside China. Ask for the harvest date and buy the newest spring lot. Trying it next to Long Jing is a good way to see how much the region changes a similar shape.
history: Jinshan Cuiya is recent. Trial production began in 1982 at the Xiashu and Wuzhou tea farms and other units in Zhenjiang, and in 1985 it passed technical appraisal and became a provincial famous tea. That same year it was named a Chinese famous tea at a national selection held by the agriculture ministry.
